newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Azov shipping wants to privatise by 1997.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Azov shipping wants to privatise by 1997.

text.p: Ukraine's Azov shipping company hopes its privatisation will be completed by the end of next year despite a row with the Transport Ministry about the valuation of its assets, a company official said late on Monday.

"We are trying to privatise by the end of next year, which will help us attract investment and bank loans to refurbish our fleet," deputy chief executive, Serhiy Rozhkov, said by telephone from the eastern port city of Mykolayiv.

He said Azov's workers were entitled to a 50 percent stake, while the government was proposing to keep 26 percent and the balance would be offered for private investment and in exchange for privatisation certificates.
He did not say what percentage of shares would be offered to private investors.
Rozhkov blamed the ministry for slowing the process because it wanted to evaluate assets of OP Azovske Morske Paroplavstvo at world prices.

"We are against this because it goes against the Ukrainian way of doing things," he said, adding that the government had turned the matter over to the State Property Fund (FDM), the state privatisation agency, to work out plans.
Attempts to issue shares in the enterprise have been going on for two years, he said.
Azov's profits halved to 2.7 million hryvnia in the first nine months of this year from 5.4 million hryvnia in the same period in 1995, Transport Ministry figures show.
Rozhkov said the company had been hit by a decline in world prices for shipping contracts.
Azov's fleet consists of 80 carriers and two tankers with an average age of 20 years.
